---
title: biblint
subtitle: Deterministic BibTeX linting and formatting
---

`biblint` checks BibTeX files for syntax and bibliography problems, then formats them into a consistent representation.
Keep the configuration in your repository so local runs and CI use the same policy.

::: {.callout-note}

## New here?

Start with `biblint check .`.
It scans the current project without changing any files.
The path is optional: `.` is the default.

:::

## A safe first workflow

### 1. Check the project

Run the linter from the project root.
A directory is searched recursively for `.bib` files, and the default-enabled rules run automatically unless your configuration selects a different set.

```console
biblint check .
```

### 2. Preview formatting

Use `--diff` when you want to inspect the formatter's exact changes.
This command does not write files.

```console
biblint format . --diff
```

### 3. Apply the profile

After reviewing the diff, format the project in place:

```console
biblint format .
```

If you want biblint to make only safe changes while checking, use `check --format --fix`.
Content-changing transforms remain disabled unless you explicitly add `--unsafe-fixes`.

## Pick the command by goal

| I want to…                        | Use  | What happens                                       |
| --------------------------------- | ---- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Find syntax and lint issues       | `biblint check .` | Reports diagnostics; writes nothing.               |
| Include formatting in the check   | `biblint check . --format` | Adds a formatting diagnostic; writes nothing.      |
| Fix safe issues automatically     | `biblint check . --format --fix` | Writes safe fixes, including formatting.           |
| Format files directly             | `biblint format .` | Writes the configured representation.              |
| Gate formatting in CI             | `biblint format . --check` | Reports files that would change and exits nonzero. |
| Review a formatting diff          | `biblint format . --diff` | Prints a unified diff and writes nothing.          |
| Integrate diagnostics with a tool | `biblint check . --output json` | Prints diagnostics as JSON.                        |
| Learn about a rule                | `biblint rule <name>` | Prints that rule's summary and fix status.         |

## What biblint reads

- A directory contributes `.bib` files recursively.
- An explicit file is checked even if its extension is not `.bib`.
- `-` reads one BibTeX document from standard input.
- `biblint.toml` is discovered by searching upward from the first input path.

See [Configuration](configuration.qmd) for include/exclude patterns and rule selection.
See [Formatting](formatting.qmd) for the changes made by default and the transforms you can opt into.

::: {.callout-warning}

## Before enabling transforms

Formatting is intentionally conservative by default.
Options such as citekey generation, merging, field removal, brace removal, and author truncation can change content or citation identity.
Preview them with `biblint format <path> --diff` before writing, and use `--unsafe-fixes` when applying them through `check --format --fix`.

:::
